findings.title: VTY lines permit Telnet
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.5 - Set transport input ssh on VTY lines
findings.remediation_template:
line vty 0 4
 transport input ssh
findings.explanation: Telnet carries usernames and passwords in cleartext. Any device on the path between an administrator and this router can read the enable password and take control. Restrict VTY transport to SSH only.

findings.title: HTTP management server enabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.2.1 - Disable the HTTP server
findings.remediation_template: no ip http server
findings.explanation: The unencrypted web management interface is running. Credentials submitted to it travel in cleartext, and the HTTP server has historically been a source of remote code execution vulnerabilities.

findings.title: VTY session timeout disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.6 - Set exec-timeout to 10 minutes or less
findings.remediation_template:
line vty 0 4
 exec-timeout 10 0
findings.explanation: exec-timeout 0 0 disables the idle timer, so an abandoned session stays authenticated indefinitely and can be reused by anyone with access to that terminal.

findings.title: VTY lines have no access-class restriction
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.4 - Apply an access-class to VTY lines
findings.remediation_template:
ip access-list standard MGMT-HOSTS
 permit 10.10.0.0 0.0.0.255
line vty 0 4
 access-class MGMT-HOSTS in
findings.explanation: No ACL limits who may open a management session, so the management plane is reachable from every network that can route to this device, including the WAN interface.

findings.title: Password encryption service disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.3 - Enable service password-encryption
findings.remediation_template: service password-encryption
findings.explanation: Passwords that have no stronger option are written to the configuration in clear text. Type 7 encryption is reversible and is not a substitute for secret hashes, but it removes casual config-backup exposure.

findings.title: Enable password stored unencrypted
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.1 - Use enable secret instead of enable password
findings.remediation_template:
no enable password
enable secret <strong-password>
findings.explanation: The privileged-EXEC password is stored in the configuration in plaintext, so anyone who can read a config backup, a TFTP transfer or an SNMP dump holds full administrative control.

findings.title: Privilege-15 local user with unencrypted password
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.2 - Store local user passwords using irreversible encryption
findings.remediation_template:
no username admin
username admin privilege 15 secret <strong-password>
findings.explanation: This account has full administrative rights and its password is stored as type 0, meaning plaintext. Use the secret keyword so the password is hashed.

findings.title: Default SNMP read-only community string
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 2.2.1 - Do not use default SNMP community strings
findings.remediation_template: no snmp-server community public RO
findings.explanation: The community string 'public' is the first value any scanner tries. It exposes the full running configuration, interface list, routing table and ARP cache to anyone who can reach UDP/161.

findings.title: SNMP read-write community uses a default string
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 2.2.2 - Do not use default or read-write SNMP community strings
findings.remediation_template: no snmp-server community private RW
findings.explanation: A read-write community is a guessable credential that permits configuration changes over UDP with no logging and no session. This is remote device control, not monitoring.

findings.title: No syslog server configured
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 3.1.1 - Configure a remote syslog host
findings.remediation_template:
logging host 10.10.0.200
logging trap informational
findings.explanation: Nothing is sent off-box, so administrative logins and configuration changes exist only in a buffer that is cleared on reboot and editable by anyone with privileged access.

findings.title: NTP not authenticated
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 3.2.1 - Use authenticated NTP
findings.remediation_template:
ntp authenticate
ntp authentication-key 1 md5 <key>
ntp trusted-key 1
ntp server 10.10.0.250 key 1
findings.explanation: Time is accepted from an unauthenticated source. An attacker who can spoof NTP can shift the clock and desynchronise every timestamp used to correlate logs during an investigation.

findings.title: AAA not enabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.3.1 - Enable AAA
findings.remediation_template:
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group tacacs+
findings.explanation: Authentication falls back to shared local passwords, so administrator actions cannot be attributed to an individual and revoking one person's access means changing credentials for everyone.

findings.title: No login banner configured
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.4.1 - Configure a login banner
findings.remediation_template:
banner login ^C
Authorised access only. Activity is monitored.
^C
findings.explanation: No warning banner is presented before authentication. Beyond the hardening benchmark, this weakens the legal position when pursuing unauthorised access.

findings.title: CDP enabled globally
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 2.1.1 - Disable CDP where not required
findings.remediation_template: no cdp run
findings.explanation: CDP advertises the model, IOS version, management address and native VLAN to any directly connected device, handing an attacker on the local segment a free inventory.

findings.title: SSH version 2 not enforced
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.2.3 - Set ip ssh version 2
findings.remediation_template:
ip ssh version 2
ip ssh time-out 60
ip ssh authentication-retries 3
findings.explanation: With no explicit version the device may negotiate SSHv1, which has known integrity weaknesses and is downgradeable by an on-path attacker.

findings.title: SNMP v1/v2c community strings in use
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 2.2.0 - Use SNMPv3
findings.remediation_template: Configure snmp-server group with v3 auth and priv
findings.explanation: SNMP v1 and v2c transmit community strings in plaintext. An attacker capturing traffic can gain full read or write access to the device configuration.

findings.title: SSH session timeout too high
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.2.4 - Set SSH timeout to 60 seconds or less
findings.remediation_template: ip ssh time-out 60
findings.explanation: Excessively long timeouts leave authenticated sessions open longer than necessary, increasing the risk of session hijacking if a terminal is left unattended.

findings.title: IP source routing enabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.6.1 - Disable IP source routing
findings.remediation_template: no ip source-route
findings.explanation: Source routing allows a sender to specify the path a packet takes. This can be used by attackers to bypass security controls or map internal network topology.

findings.title: No MOTD banner configured
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.4.2 - Configure a Message of the Day (MOTD) banner
findings.remediation_template: banner motd ^C Authorized Access Only ^C
findings.explanation: A MOTD banner provides a legal warning to unauthorized users. Without it, it is harder to prosecute unauthorized access in many legal jurisdictions.

findings.title: AAA login authentication not configured
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.2 - Enable 'aaa authentication login'
findings.remediation_template: aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local
findings.explanation: Without AAA login authentication, the device may fall back to insecure local passwords or no authentication at all.

findings.title: AAA enable authentication not configured
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.3 - Enable 'aaa authentication enable default'
findings.remediation_template: aaa authentication enable default group tacacs+ enable
findings.explanation: Privileged EXEC mode must be protected by AAA to ensure that only authorized administrators can enter enable mode.

findings.title: AAA command accounting disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.6 - Set 'aaa accounting' to log all privileged use commands
findings.remediation_template: aaa accounting commands 15 default start-stop group tacacs+
findings.explanation: Accounting for privilege 15 commands is essential for forensic audits to see exactly what changes were made by which administrator.

findings.title: AAA connection accounting disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.7 - Set 'aaa accounting connection'
findings.remediation_template: aaa accounting connection default start-stop group tacacs+
findings.explanation: Connection accounting tracks the start and end of sessions, helping to identify session hijacking or unusual login patterns.

findings.title: AAA exec accounting disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.8 - Set 'aaa accounting exec'
findings.remediation_template: aaa accounting exec default start-stop group tacacs+
findings.explanation: Exec accounting logs the start and end of the shell session itself.

findings.title: AAA network accounting disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.9 - Set 'aaa accounting network'
findings.remediation_template: aaa accounting network default start-stop group tacacs+
findings.explanation: Network accounting tracks network-related service requests.

findings.title: AAA system accounting disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.1.10 - Set 'aaa accounting system'
findings.remediation_template: aaa accounting system default start-stop group tacacs+
findings.explanation: System accounting logs events not associated with users, such as system reloads.

findings.title: Local users have excessive privileges
findings.cis_control: CIS Cisco IOS 1.2.1 - Set 'privilege 1' for local users
findings.remediation_template: username <user> privilege 1
findings.explanation: Local accounts should be restricted to privilege 1. Administrative access should be gained via the 'enable' command to ensure a second layer of auth.

attack_paths.name: Cleartext management plane to privileged takeover
attack_paths.narrative: In this attack path, an attacker exploits exposed network management interfaces to intercept cleartext traffic and leverage credential weaknesses for a full administrative takeover. The findings chain together because open access allows unauthorized users to reach unencrypted protocols like Telnet and exploit weak configurations to capture sensitive data and escalate privileges. Implementing an access-class restriction breaks this chain by completely blocking unauthorized reachability to all management protocols at once. By shutting off this network access, the remaining protocol and credential vulnerabilities become unreachable and cannot be exploited while permanent fixes are put in place.

break_chain.why: Applying an access-class removes reachability for every management protocol at once, so the Telnet and credential weaknesses become unreachable while they are being fixed.

attack_paths.name: SNMP reconnaissance to device control
attack_paths.narrative: An attacker exploits weak SNMP network configurations to first discover vulnerable devices and then abuse read-write access to gain full control over the hardware. These findings chain together as initial information-gathering vulnerabilities allow the attacker to locate the target, while permissive credentials enable them to alter the device's settings. The break-chain fix disrupts this path by disabling the read-write SNMP community string, preventing the attacker from executing commands or modifying configuration files. By stripping away write permissions, this fix ensures that even if an attacker discovers the device, they cannot escalate the intrusion from minor data exposure to a full network outage.

break_chain.why: Removing the read-write community reduces the worst case from device control to information disclosure, which is the difference between an incident and an outage.

attack_paths.name: Configuration read to credential reuse
attack_paths.narrative: In this attack path, an attacker first gains access to a network device's configuration file. Because the device configuration contains plain-text passwords, the attacker can easily extract these credentials and reuse them to gain administrative control over other systems. Implementing the recommended fix updates the configuration to store passwords as secure, irreversible hashes rather than readable text. This breaks the attack path because reading the configuration file will no longer provide the attacker with usable credentials to escalate their privileges.

break_chain.why: Moving to enable secret replaces a readable password with an irreversible hash, so reading the configuration no longer yields privileged access.
